items.stem: An elderly woman presents with a fall and a tender right hip. Which of the following is true regarding the hip and neck of femur (NOF) fractures?
options: Limb shortening in NOF fracture is uncommon.
The lateral circumflex artery supplies the majority of blood to the femoral head.
Metaphyseal blood supply arises from the extracapsular arterial ring.
Extracapsular fractures commonly compromise the blood supply.
The artery of ligamentum teres is the main blood supply to the hip joint.
items.answer_text: Metaphyseal blood supply arises from the extracapsular arterial ring.
items.explanation: Limb shortening is a common feature of neck of femur (NOF) fracture and is pathognomonic. The blood supply to the femoral head is of note as fractures of the femoral neck are likely to disrupt the blood supply and lead to avascular necrosis. The medial and lateral circumflex arteries supply the extracapsular arterial ring, with the medial artery being the most important. From the arterial ring, delicate retinacular vessels pass underneath the capsular and up the femoral neck into the head.

items.stem: An obese 15-year-old boy presents with pain in the hip. He walks with an antalgic gait with some shortening of the affected limb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Perthes disease
Congenital hip dysplasia
Septic arthritis
Neck of femur fracture
Slipped upper femoral epiphysis (SUFE)
items.explanation: Slipped upper femoral epiphysis (SUFE) most commonly affects overweight boys around the age of puberty (10–15 years). Perthes disease more commonly affects boys but presents earlier (4–10 years). Septic arthritis and neck of femur fractures are incredibly rare in this age of patient and the patient is unlikely to be able to bear weight. Congenital hip dysplasia is a disease that presents in the newborn or is diagnosed in the first few years of life (0–5 years).

items.stem: If concerned about compartment syndrome following reperfusion of the lower leg, what action would you perform in order to test the deep part of the posterior compartment of the lower leg?
options: Plantarflexion of the foot
Eversion of the foot
Extension of the great toe
Dorsiflexion of the foot
Flexion of the 2nd to 5th toes
items.explanation:
If you suspect a patient with compartment syndrome in the lower leg, it is important to be able to clinically isolate all four compartments. Pain on a passive stretch of a muscle is a key diagnostic sign in compartment syndrome. The following are the isolated passive movements for each compartment:

Anterior – foot plantarflexion Lateral – foot inversion Superficial posterior – foot dorsiflexion Deep posterior – great toe extension

Compartment syndrome develops when oedema creates venous occlusion leading to tissue injury and further oedema. Subsequently, pressure within the compartment builds until the arterial supply is compromised, resulting in tissue death.

items.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the hamstring muscles is incorrect?
options: The hamstring muscles arise from the ischial tuberosity.
Semimembranosus inserts on the medial condyle of the tibia.
The short head of biceps femoris originates from the linea aspera.
All three muscles are supplied by the sciatic nerve.
The hamstring compartment receives its blood supply from the femoral artery.
items.answer_text: The hamstring compartment receives its blood supply from the femoral artery.
items.explanation: Semitendinosus originates from the medial aspect of the ischial tuberosity and inserts deep to the gracilis on the upper part of the tibia. The long head of the biceps femoris also originates from the ischial tuberosity and the short head originates from the linea aspera. Both heads form one single tendon inserting into the head of the fibula. The hamstring compartment receives its blood supply from the profunda femoris artery.

items.stem: Concerning the blood supply to the femoral head, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The arterial supply from the ligamentum teres contributes more significantly in adulthood.
The main blood supply is derived from the obturator artery in the adult.
Lateral and medial circumflex femoral arteries supply the femoral head via retinacula.
Vessels from the diaphysis of cancellous bone provide a negligible arterial blood supply in adulthood.
Fractures that are extracapsular have a high risk of resulting in avascular necrosis.
items.answer_text: Lateral and medial circumflex femoral arteries supply the femoral head via retinacula.
items.explanation: The arterial supply from the ligamentum teres contributes more significantly in childhood. The obturator artery gives off a branch via the ligamentum teres, which provides a negligible blood supply to the femoral head in adults. Lateral and medial circumflex femoral arteries supply the femoral head via retinacula, which reflect back in longitudinal bands under the hip capsule. Vessels from the diaphysis of cancellous bone provide a small arterial blood supply in adulthood.

items.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the popliteal fossa is correct?
options: The superior and medial boundary is the biceps femoris.
The roof contains the terminal branch of the posterior cutaneous nerve.
The floor contains the oblique popliteal ligament.
The capsule of the knee joint is found in the roof of the fossa.
The small saphenous vein is found in the floor of the fossa.
items.answer_text: The floor contains the oblique popliteal ligament.
items.explanation:
The popliteal fossa is a space located at the back of the knee joint. The boundaries are:

Superior and medial – semitendinosus Superior and lateral – biceps femoris Inferior and medial – medial head of gastrocnemius Inferior and lateral – lateral head of gastrocnemius Roof – deep fascia Floor – popliteal surface of the femur, capsule of knee joint and oblique popliteal ligament

The contents include popliteal artery, popliteal vein, tibial nerve, common peroneal nerve and popliteal lymph nodes.

items.stem: The lower limb below the knee is divided into four compartments. Which of the following statements regarding these compartments is incorrect?
options: The lateral compartment contains the peroneus longus, brevis and tibialis anterior muscles.
The superficial posterior compartment contains the plantaris muscle and soleus.
The anterior compartment contains the anterior tibial vessels and tibial nerve.
The lateral compartment contains the deep peroneal nerve.
The deep posterior compartment contains the flexor hallucis longus, flexor digitorum longus and peroneus tertius.
items.answer_text: The superficial posterior compartment contains the plantaris muscle and soleus.
items.explanation: The anterior compartment contains the tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus and peroneus tertius muscles along with the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels. The lateral compartment contains peroneus longus and brevis muscles along with the superficial peroneal nerve and perforations from the peroneal artery. The deep posterior compartment contains tibialis posterior, flexor hallucis longus, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial and peroneal arteries and the tibial nerve. The superficial posterior compartment contains soleus, gastrocnemius and plantaris muscles and the medial cutaneous sural nerve.

items.stem: A middle-aged woman undergoes surgery for varicose veins. A saphenofemoral junction ligation is performed. Which of the following tributaries does not commonly join the long saphenous vein at the opening?
options: Superficial epigastric vein
Superficial external pudendal vein
Superficial circumflex iliac vein
Inferior epigastric vein
Deep external pudendal vein
items.explanation: The long saphenous vein drains the medial end of the dorsal venous arch of the foot. It passes anterior to the medial malleolus ascending the medial side of the leg with the saphenous nerve. It crosses the knee a palm’s breadth medial to the patella and passes along the medial aspect of the thigh through the lower part of the saphenous opening in the cribriform fascia to join the femoral vein 2 cm below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. There are usually four veins that join the long saphenous vein in the region of the saphenous opening: the superficial epigastric vein, superficial external pudendal vein, deep external pudendal vein and superficial circumflex iliac vein.

items.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the tibial nerve is correct?
options: Cutaneous supply within the popliteal fossa is via a branch of the sural nerve.
The roots of the tibial nerve are L3, L4, L5, S1, S2.
The nerve descends superficial to soleus in the calf.
The nerve divides into the medial and lateral tibial nerves in the foot.
It does not supply the extrinsic muscles of the foot.
items.answer_text: Cutaneous supply within the popliteal fossa is via a branch of the sural nerve.
items.explanation: The tibial nerve originates from the roots L4, 5, S1, 2, 3. It traverses the popliteal fossa and descends in the calf deep to the soleus. It is accompanied by the posterior tibial vessels, passes behind the medial malleolus and ends by dividing into the medial and lateral plantar nerves in the foot. In the popliteal fossa muscular branches are given to gastrocnemius, popliteus and soleus with a cutaneous branch of the sural nerve.
